course.title: 3rd grade
course.lead: The numbers grow bigger, but you keep the same method: observe, represent, calculate, check, explain. Your progress is saved on this device.

yamba.name: Yamba
yamba.courseWelcome: Welcome to the middle grades! I'm staying right by your side, at your own pace.
yamba.lessonTip: Take your time, use real objects if that helps. I'm staying close for this first step.
yamba.lessonComplete: Well done! Your progress is saved, come back whenever you like.

Finally, I write an answer sentence.

u01l01.objective: I can build a number using place value.
u01l01.situation: The class gathers 246 seeds to prepare small bags. How can they be counted quickly?
u01l01.discover: Ten units make a ten; ten tens make a hundred. In 246, the 2 is worth 200, the 4 is worth 40 and the 6 is worth 6.

manipulate.title: Build the number 324
manipulate.instruction: Build 324 using hundred blocks, ten sticks and single units.
manipulate.hint: Start with the hundreds: how many hundred blocks are needed?
manipulate.strongHint: 324 is 3 hundred blocks, 2 ten sticks and 4 units. Adjust each counter one at a time.

example.medium: Intermediate. What number is made of 8 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 units?
example.reflection: Reflection. In 609, what is the value of the digit 6?

practice.title: Break down 572
practice.instruction: Build 572 with blocks, sticks and units, just like in the guided example.
practice.hint: Look at each digit of 572: hundreds, then tens, then units.

reflect.title: Which number is it?
reflect.instruction: Work out the number from its breakdown, then write it in digits.
reflect.hint: Add the hundreds first, then the tens, then the units.
reflect.strongHint: 8 hundreds make 800, 3 tens make 30, and there are 5 units left: 800 + 30 + 5.
reflect.prompt: What number is made of 8 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 units?

play.title: Deliver to the right depot
play.instruction: Deliver the hundreds, tens and units of 463 to the right depot by building the number.
play.hint: Place the hundred blocks first, then the ten sticks, then the units.
play.strongHint: 463 is 4 hundred blocks, 6 ten sticks and 3 units.

u01l01.remember: Ten units make a ten; ten tens make a hundred.

check.title: What is the highlighted digit worth?
check.instruction: Choose the exact value of the hundreds digit in 609.
check.hint: This digit sits in the hundreds place: it isn't just worth itself.
check.strongHint: In 609, the 6 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 600.
check.prompt: In 609, what is the value of the digit 6?

u01l02.objective: I can move from words to digits.
u01l02.situation: A card reads "four hundred and thirty-two" drawn bags.
u01l02.discover: We spot the hundreds, then the tens and the units. An empty place is written with 0: six hundred and five is written 605.

manipulate.title: Listen and build
manipulate.instruction: Build each number you are given, with blocks, sticks and units: 407, then 760, then 999.
manipulate.hint: An empty place is written with 0: don't add a ten stick if there isn't one.
manipulate.strongHint: 407 = 4 hundreds, 0 tens, 7 units. Check each number digit by digit.

example.easy: Easy. Write in digits: three hundred and twenty-eight.
example.medium: Intermediate. Write 904 in words.
example.reflection: Reflection. Write the number made of 5 hundreds and 7 units.

practice.title: Words and digits
practice.instruction: Match each number to its correct word form, or each word form to its number.
practice.hint: Spot the hundreds first, in the words or in the digits.
practice.strongHint: Three hundred and twenty-eight = 3 hundreds, 2 tens and 8 units, so 328.

reflect.title: Find the number
reflect.instruction: Work out the number from its breakdown, then write it in digits.
reflect.hint: 5 hundreds and 7 units: there is no ten, so 0 tens.
reflect.strongHint: 5 hundreds make 500, 0 tens, and 7 units: 500 + 0 + 7 = 507.
reflect.prompt: Write the number made of 5 hundreds and 7 units.

play.title: Match the number card
play.instruction: Match each word form to its number card, or each number card to its word form.
play.hint: Count the hundreds in the word form before choosing.
play.strongHint: Read the number digit by digit: hundreds, then tens, then units.

u01l02.remember: We spot the hundreds, then the tens and the units.

check.title: Build the announced number
check.instruction: Build 693 with blocks, sticks and units.
check.hint: 693: how many hundreds, tens and units?

u01l03.situation: Two storehouses show 487 and 509 bags. Which one has more?
u01l03.discover: We compare the hundreds first, then the tens, then the units.

manipulate.title: Build, then compare
manipulate.instruction: Build 438, then 483, and look at the first place where they differ.
manipulate.hint: The hundreds are the same: look at the tens.
manipulate.strongHint: 438 has 3 tens, 483 has 8 tens: so 483 is bigger.

example.medium: Intermediate. Order 312, 132, 321, 213.
example.reflection: Reflection. Find two numbers between 495 and 500.

practice.title: Compare the numbers
practice.instruction: Choose the symbol that correctly compares each pair of numbers.
practice.hint: Compare the hundreds digit of each number first.
practice.strongHint: If the hundreds are equal, compare the tens, then the units.

reflect.title: Order the numbers
reflect.instruction: Place the four numbers from smallest to largest.
reflect.hint: Start by spotting the smallest hundreds digit.
reflect.strongHint: 132 has 1 hundred, 213 has 2, 312 and 321 have 3: compare their tens next.

play.title: The canoe race
play.instruction: Move forward the canoe carrying the bigger number in each round.
play.hint: Look at the hundreds of each number first.
play.strongHint: Compare hundreds, then tens, then units to find the bigger number.

u01l03.remember: We compare the hundreds first, then the tens, then the units.

check.title: Find a hidden number
check.instruction: Write a whole number that is strictly between the two limits.
check.hint: 495 and 500 don't count: look for a number in between.
check.strongHint: Between 495 and 500, you can choose 496, 497, 498 or 499.

u01l04.objective: I can spot a pattern and estimate.
u01l04.situation: The markers along a path show 200, 250, 300, then one sign is missing.
u01l04.discover: A pattern moves forward following a rule. To round to the nearest ten, we choose the closest ten.

manipulate.title: Continue the pattern
manipulate.instruction: Continue the pattern counting up by 25 using place-value cards.
manipulate.hint: Look at how much the pattern moves forward each time.
manipulate.strongHint: The pattern moves forward by 50 each time: 200, 250, 300, then 350.

example.medium: Intermediate. Round 63 to the nearest ten.
example.reflection: Reflection. What rule does 105, 205, 305, 405 follow?

practice.title: Complete the pattern
practice.instruction: Find the missing number in the pattern.
practice.hint: Look at the gap between the numbers you already know.
practice.strongHint: The pattern moves forward by 10 each time: after 350 comes 360.

reflect.title: Round to the nearest ten
reflect.instruction: Choose the ten closest to the given number.
reflect.hint: Look at the units digit: is it closer to 0 or to 10?
reflect.strongHint: 63 is closer to 60 than to 70, because 3 is closer to 0 than to 10.

play.title: Repair the number path
play.instruction: Repair the path by finding the missing number in the pattern.
play.hint: Compare the two known numbers to find the pattern's step.
play.strongHint: The path moves forward by 100 each time: after 600 comes 700.

u01l04.remember: A pattern moves forward following a rule.

check.title: Discover the rule
check.instruction: Choose the step that explains this number pattern.
check.hint: Work out the gap between two neighbouring numbers in the pattern.
check.prompt: In the sequence 105, 205, 305, 405, by how much does each number go up?

u01eval.intro: Work on your own first. Use a drawing if you need to, and explain at least one answer.

q1.title: Question 1
q1.instruction: Work out the number from its breakdown.
q1.hint: Add the hundreds, the tens, then the units.
q1.strongHint: 8 hundreds make 800, 3 tens make 30, and there are 5 units left: 800 + 30 + 5.
q1.prompt: What number is made of 8 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 units?

q2.title: Question 2
q2.instruction: Choose the word form that matches the number shown exactly.
q2.hint: Spot the hundreds first: nine hundred.
q2.strongHint: 904 = nine hundred and four: there are no tens.

q3.title: Question 3
q3.instruction: Place the four numbers from smallest to largest.
q3.hint: Compare the hundreds digit of each number first.
q3.strongHint: 132 has 1 hundred, 213 has 2, 312 and 321 have 3: compare their tens next.

q4.title: Question 4
q4.instruction: Choose the ten closest to the given number.
q4.hint: Look at the units digit: is it closer to 0 or to 10?

instruction.numeric: Work it out, then write your answer.
instruction.numericChoice: Work it out, then pick the right answer.
instruction.choice: Read carefully, then pick the right answer.
instruction.placeValue: Build the number with hundreds, tens and ones.
instruction.column: Set out the operation and write the result digit by digit.
instruction.groups: Build the equal groups you are asked for.
instruction.share: Share the tokens between the bowls, then note what is left.
instruction.money: Place cards to make exactly the amount you are asked for.
instruction.fraction: Colour the right number of parts.
instruction.clock: Turn the hands to show the time you are asked for.
instruction.grid: Guide the counter with the arrows to the target square.
instruction.steps: Tap the steps in the right order.
instruction.compare: Choose the right symbol for each pair.
instruction.order: Put the numbers in the order asked for.

u02l01.objective: I can break numbers apart to add quickly.
u02l01.situation: A team collects 120 bottle tops, then 35 more. How can you find the total without counting everything again?
u02l01.discover: You can split hundreds, tens and ones, then put the results back together. 120 + 35: 100 + 20 + 30 + 5 = 155.

manipulate.hint: Start with the hundreds: how many are in 230?
manipulate.strongHint: 230 + 40 + 6: 2 hundreds, 7 tens (3 + 4) and 6 ones, so 276.
manipulate.instruction: Build 230 + 40 + 6 with hundreds, tens and ones.

example.reflection: Think. Work out 198 + 6 by going through 200.

practice.hint: Only the tens change: 4 tens + 2 tens.
practice.strongHint: 145 + 20: hundreds and ones stay the same, 4 tens + 2 tens = 6 tens. The answer is 165.
practice.prompt: Work out 145 + 20.

reflect.hint: From 198 to 200 you add 2. How much of the 6 is left to add?
reflect.prompt: Work out 198 + 6 by going through 200. What is the result?

play.hint: 35 splits into 30 and 5.
play.prompt: To work out 120 + 35 on the number line, which jumps do you choose?
play.c0: A jump of 300, then a jump of 5
play.c1: A jump of 30, then a jump of 5
play.c2: A jump of 3, then a jump of 5

u02l01.remember: You can split hundreds, tens and ones, then put the results back together.

check.prompt: Work out 120 + 35.

u02l02.objective: I can line up the place values.
u02l02.situation: Two schools put together 243 and 516 pictured notebooks. How many notebooks in all?
u02l02.discover: Line up ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds; then add each column.

manipulate.hint: Start with the ones column, on the right.
manipulate.instruction: Set out 132 + 245 on the chart and write the result column by column.

example.reflection: Think. Why do 23 and 415 not line up on the left?

practice.hint: Add the ones, then the tens, then the hundreds.

reflect.hint: Look at the column on the far right: what does it hold?
reflect.strongHint: Ones go under ones: 23 sits under the last two digits of 415.
reflect.prompt: Why do 23 and 415 not line up on the left when you set out the addition?
reflect.c0: Because the ones must be in the same column

play.hint: Put each digit in its column before adding.
play.title: Put the digits back

u02l02.remember: Line up ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds; then add each column.

check.prompt: Work out 405 + 172.

u02l03.objective: I can trade ten ones or ten tens.
u02l03.situation: A store receives 278 then 156 sacks. How many sacks does it have in all?
u02l03.discover: When a column reaches 10, write the ones of the result and carry one to the next place.

manipulate.hint: 8 + 7 is more than 10: trade ten ones for one ten.
manipulate.strongHint: 8 + 7 = 15: write 5 and carry 1 ten. 6 + 5 + 1 = 12: write 2 and carry 1 hundred. 1 + 1 = 2. The result is 225.
manipulate.instruction: Set out 168 + 57 and make the trades: write the result column by column.

example.reflection: Think. Check 375 + 248 = 623 with an estimate.

practice.hint: 7 + 8 = 15: write 5 and carry one ten.
practice.strongHint: 7 + 8 = 15, I write 5 and carry 1. 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. The result is 85.

reflect.hint: Round each number to the nearest easy landmark.
reflect.strongHint: 375 is close to 400 and 248 to 250: about 650, so 623 is believable.
reflect.prompt: To check 375 + 248 = 623, which estimate is closest?

play.hint: Trade ten tokens before filling in the next column.
play.title: Trade before you go on

u02l03.remember: When a column reaches 10, write the ones of the result and carry one to the next place.

check.hint: Start with 8 + 6 in the ones column.
check.prompt: How many sacks in all: 278 sacks and 156 sacks?

u02l04.objective: I can recognise putting together or an increase.
u02l04.situation: A class library has 356 pictured books and receives 128 more. How many books does it have now?
u02l04.discover: Find what is put together or added, work it out, then answer with the unit.

manipulate.hint: Two bars placed end to end: the amounts are put together.
manipulate.strongHint: Putting two amounts together means adding: 356 + 128.
manipulate.title: I draw it with bars
manipulate.prompt: A bar diagram shows a bar of 356 books and a bar of 128 books placed end to end. Which calculation does it show?

example.medium: Medium. A bus has 38 passengers; 17 get on. How many now?
example.reflection: Think. Make up a problem whose calculation is 325 + 75.

practice.hint: Two amounts are put together: which operation?
practice.prompt: 245 mangoes and 176 mangoes: how many mangoes in all?

reflect.hint: Passengers get on: the amount goes up.
reflect.strongHint: 38 + 17 = 55 passengers.
reflect.prompt: A bus has 38 passengers; 17 get on. How many passengers are there now?

play.hint: The question is only about mangoes.
play.strongHint: Keep the mangoes: 120 and 30. The 45 bananas are not needed.
play.title: Pick the useful information
play.prompt: "A trader has 120 mangoes and 45 bananas. He receives 30 mangoes. How many mangoes does he have now?" Which pieces of information are useful?

u02l04.remember: Find what is put together or added, work it out, then answer with the unit.

check.prompt: A problem has the calculation 325 + 75. What is the result?

u02eval.intro: Work alone first. Use a diagram if you need one and explain at least one answer.

q2.hint: Line up the places: ones under ones.

q3.hint: Think about carrying: 6 + 9 is more than 10.

q4.prompt: A bus has 38 passengers; 17 get on. How many passengers now?

u03l01.objective: I can break numbers apart to subtract.
u03l01.situation: A basket holds 460 seeds; 30 are used. How many seeds are left?
u03l01.discover: You can take away hundreds, tens or ones first, depending on the numbers. 460 − 30: 6 tens minus 3 tens.

manipulate.hint: Start from 380: 8 tens. How many are left when you take 4 away?
manipulate.strongHint: 380 − 40: 8 tens − 4 tens = 4 tens. The result is 340.
manipulate.instruction: Work out 380 − 40 with bundles of ten, then build the result.

example.reflection: Think. Work out 402 − 5 by going through 400.

practice.hint: Only the tens change: 8 tens − 2 tens.
practice.prompt: Work out 286 − 20.

reflect.hint: From 402 to 400 you go back 2. How much is left to go back?
reflect.prompt: Work out 402 − 5 by going through 400. What is the result?

play.hint: Compare the tens: 6 and 3.
play.title: Jump back efficiently
play.prompt: To go back from 460 to 430 on the number line, which jump do you make?

u03l01.remember: You can take away hundreds, tens or ones first, depending on the numbers.

check.prompt: Work out 700 − 200.

u03l02.objective: I can line up and subtract place by place.
u03l02.situation: A store has 758 pictured notebooks and gives out 326. How many notebooks are left?
u03l02.discover: Line up the places and subtract from right to left: ones, then tens, then hundreds.

manipulate.hint: Start with the ones column, on the right.
manipulate.instruction: Set out 674 − 231 on the chart and write the result column by column.

example.reflection: Think. Check 742 − 321 = 421.

practice.hint: Subtract the ones, then the tens, then the hundreds.

reflect.hint: If you take a number away and put it back, you are back where you started.
reflect.strongHint: Check by adding back what you took away: 421 + 321 = 742.
reflect.prompt: How can you check that 742 − 321 = 421?

play.hint: Unload each column of the lorry one at a time, starting with the ones.
play.title: Unload each column

u03l02.remember: Line up the places and subtract from right to left.

check.hint: The ones are 0 and 0. Move to the tens: 9 − 7.
check.prompt: Work out 590 − 170.

u03l03.objective: I can trade a ten or a hundred.
u03l03.situation: We want to take 47 away from 132, but 2 ones are not enough to take away 7. What can we do?
u03l03.discover: Trade one ten for 10 ones. If there is no ten left, trade a hundred first.

manipulate.hint: 2 − 7 is impossible: trade one ten for 10 ones.
manipulate.strongHint: 12 − 7 = 5; 2 tens are left, 2 − 4 is impossible: trade 1 hundred, 12 − 4 = 8; 0 hundreds are left. The result is 85.
manipulate.instruction: Show 132 − 47, make the trades and write the result column by column.

example.reflection: Think. Explain the trade in 502 − 178.

practice.hint: 2 − 8 is impossible: trade a ten.
practice.strongHint: 12 − 8 = 4; 6 tens are left, 6 − 3 = 3. The result is 34.

reflect.hint: There are no tens in 502: where will the ones come from?
reflect.strongHint: Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens, then 1 ten for 10 ones; the result is 324.
reflect.prompt: In 502 − 178, what do you do first?
reflect.c0: I trade a hundred for 10 tens, then a ten for 10 ones
reflect.c1: I take the smaller digit from the larger one in each column
reflect.c2: I take away 5 hundreds straight away

play.hint: Trade without changing the total: a hundred is worth 10 tens.
play.strongHint: 300 = 2 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones. 10 − 6 = 4; 9 − 2 = 7; 2 − 1 = 1. The result is 174.
play.title: Make the trades

u03l03.remember: Trade one ten for 10 ones. If there is no ten left, trade a hundred first.

check.strongHint: 11 − 8 = 3; 3 − 6 is impossible, trade a hundred: 13 − 6 = 7; 1 − 0 = 1. The result is 173.
check.prompt: Work out 241 − 68.

u03l04.objective: I can choose between difference and complement.
u03l04.situation: Two teams have 615 and 487 points. What is the gap between them?
u03l04.discover: For a gap, subtract the smaller from the larger. To complete, find what must be added.

manipulate.hint: Move in steps: 480 → 500, then 500 → 600, then 600 → 615.
manipulate.title: I measure the gap on the line
manipulate.prompt: On the number line, what is the distance from 480 to 615?

example.reflection: Think. An amount drops from 742 to 598. By how much?

practice.hint: Subtract the smaller from the larger.
practice.prompt: What is the difference between 900 and 675?

reflect.hint: Find the gap between 742 and 598.
reflect.prompt: An amount drops from 742 to 598. By how much did it drop?

play.hint: Gap = larger number − smaller number.
play.title: Even out two stores
play.prompt: Two stores hold 340 and 290. By how much does the larger exceed the smaller?

u03l04.remember: For a gap, subtract the smaller from the larger. To complete, find what must be added.

check.hint: Find what must be added to 185 to reach 500.
check.prompt: Find the missing number: __ + 185 = 500.

u03eval.intro: Work alone first. Use a diagram if you need one and explain at least one answer.

q2.hint: Line up the places, then subtract from right to left.

q3.hint: There are no tens: trade a hundred first.
q3.strongHint: 300 = 2 hundreds, 9 tens, 10 ones. The result is 174.

q4.hint: Find what to add to 185 to get 500.

u04l01.situation: Benches each have 2 seats; packs hold 5 or 10 items. How can you count the total quickly?
u04l01.discover: To multiply is to count equal groups. You can check with repeated addition: 6 × 5 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5.

manipulate.hint: You need 6 groups, with 5 seeds in each group.
manipulate.strongHint: 6 groups of 5: set "Groups" to 6 and "In one group" to 5. Total 30.
manipulate.instruction: Build 6 groups of 5 seeds: set the number of groups and what is in one group.

example.medium: Medium. 8 × 5 = __.
example.reflection: Think. How many groups of 10 make 90?

practice.hint: 7 groups of 2: count in twos.
practice.prompt: Work out 7 × 2.

reflect.hint: Count in tens up to 90.
reflect.prompt: How many groups of 10 make 90?

play.hint: Each row holds 10 items.
play.strongHint: 4 rows of 10: set "Groups" to 4 and "In one group" to 10. Total 40.
play.title: Fill the rows

u04l01.remember: To multiply is to count equal groups. You can check with repeated addition.

check.prompt: Work out 8 × 5.

u04l02.situation: Four flower beds each have 3 pictured plants. How many plants in all?
u04l02.discover: You can build the table of 4 by doubling twice: 6 × 4 is double 6 × 2.

manipulate.hint: Make 7 groups, with 3 items in each group.
manipulate.instruction: Make 7 groups of 3, then read the total.

example.medium: Medium. 7 × 4 = __.
example.reflection: Think. Compare 5 × 4 and 4 × 5.

practice.hint: Count in threes six times.
practice.prompt: Work out 6 × 3.

reflect.hint: Work out each of the two products.
reflect.strongHint: 5 groups of 4 and 4 groups of 5 both make 20: the groups are just described differently.
reflect.prompt: Compare 5 × 4 and 4 × 5.

play.hint: You need 4 regular rows of 6 plants.
play.strongHint: 4 rows of 6 plants: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24.
play.title: Arrange the plants in rows
play.instruction: Arrange 24 plants in 4 regular rows of 6.

u04l02.remember: You can build the table of 4 by doubling twice: 6 × 4 is double 6 × 2.

check.prompt: Work out 7 × 4.

u04l03.objective: I can multiply a number by a small number.
u04l03.situation: Three classes each receive 124 sheets. How many sheets in all?
u04l03.discover: Multiply each place by the small number and carry when needed.

manipulate.hint: Multiply the ones first: 3 × 2.
manipulate.strongHint: 3 × 2 = 6 ones; 3 × 4 tens = 12 tens, which is 1 hundred and 2 tens. The result is 126.
manipulate.instruction: Show 3 × 42 with tens and ones, then set out 42 × 3.

example.reflection: Think. Estimate 5 × 198 before working it out.

practice.hint: Multiply the ones, then the tens.

reflect.hint: 198 is close to 200.
reflect.strongHint: 5 × 200 = 1,000: the result of 5 × 198 is a little less than 1,000.
reflect.prompt: Estimate 5 × 198 before working it out: which result is closest?

play.hint: Copy the load: 124 sheets, three times.
play.title: Copy the load

u04l03.remember: Multiply each place by the small number and carry when needed.

check.prompt: Work out 3 × 128.

u04l04.objective: I can read a division with or without a remainder.
u04l04.situation: 24 fruits are shared between 4 baskets. How many fruits in each basket?
u04l04.discover: Sharing looks for the amount in each share; grouping looks for the number of groups. A remainder is what does not make a full share.

manipulate.hint: Put one mango in each basket, again and again, as long as every basket can get one.
manipulate.strongHint: 26 mangoes in 4 baskets: 6 in each basket (24 mangoes) and 2 mangoes are left.
manipulate.instruction: Share 26 mangoes equally between 4 baskets. Leave in the starting basket what can no longer be shared.

example.easy: Easy. 32 shared between 4 gives how many each?
example.medium: Medium. How many groups of 5 in 23?
example.reflection: Think. Check 27 ÷ 3 = 9.

practice.hint: Find the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 4.
practice.prompt: 32 items are shared between 4 children. How many items does each child get?

reflect.hint: Count in fives without going past 23.
reflect.strongHint: 4 × 5 = 20; 3 items are left, which do not make a full group. You make 4 groups.
reflect.prompt: How many groups of 5 can you make with 23 items?

play.hint: Each bowl gets the same number of tokens; what is left cannot be shared out.
play.strongHint: 17 tokens in 5 bowls: 3 in each bowl (15 tokens), 2 tokens are left.
play.title: Share out as the mission says
play.instruction: Share 17 tokens between 5 bowls, then note each bowl's share and the remainder.

u04l04.remember: Sharing looks for the amount in each share; grouping looks for the number of groups.

check.hint: A division is checked with a multiplication.
check.prompt: Which multiplication confirms 27 ÷ 3 = 9?

u04eval.intro: Work alone first. Use a diagram if you need one and explain at least one answer.

q3.hint: Multiply each place by 3, starting with the ones.

q4.hint: Count in fives without going past 23.
q4.prompt: How many groups of 5 can you make from 23?

u05l01.objective: I can recognise a correct fraction.
u05l01.situation: A pictured flatbread is shared between four children. What is needed for the sharing to be fair?
u05l01.discover: A fraction describes equal parts of a whole. If the parts are not equal, they are not quarters.

manipulate.hint: Half of 4 parts is how many parts?
manipulate.strongHint: A strip of 4 equal parts: colouring half means colouring 2 parts.
manipulate.instruction: A strip is shared into 4 equal parts: colour half of the strip.

example.easy: Easy. How many halves make a whole?
example.medium: Medium. How many quarters make a whole?
example.reflection: Think. Are two unequal parts two halves?

practice.hint: One half and another half...
practice.prompt: How many halves make a whole?

reflect.hint: Think of sharing a flatbread between two friends: is it fair if one gets more?
reflect.strongHint: A half is one of two equal parts.
reflect.prompt: Are two unequal parts two halves?
reflect.c0: No: the two halves must be equal
reflect.c1: Yes: having two parts is enough
reflect.c2: Yes, if one of the two is bigger

play.hint: A quarter is one of 4 equal parts.
play.strongHint: You need 4 parts, and they must be equal.
play.title: Cut into equal parts
play.prompt: Which way of sharing a flatbread gives quarters?

u05l01.remember: A fraction describes equal parts of a whole.

check.hint: A quarter is one part out of 4.

manipulate.strongHint: 1 part out of 4 equal parts is written 1/4: colour just one square.

example.reflection: Think. Which fraction shows one part out of two?

u05l03.objective: I can compare parts of the same whole.

manipulate.hint: Picture the two coloured parts laid on top of each other.
manipulate.strongHint: The more parts there are, the smaller each part: 1/2 is bigger than 1/4.

example.medium: Medium. Complete: 1/3 __ 1/3.

reflect.hint: A fraction depends on the size of the whole.
reflect.strongHint: To compare with fractions, the wholes must be the same size.
reflect.prompt: Can you compare half of a small orange and a quarter of a very big orange using only the fractions?
reflect.c0: No: the wholes must be the same size

play.hint: The fewer the parts, the bigger each part.
play.strongHint: 1/3 is bigger than 1/4.

play.prompt: Which strip has the bigger coloured part? Do not trust the picture only: count the parts.

u05l03.remember: For the same whole, a half is bigger than a quarter.

check.hint: These are the same fraction of the same whole twice.
check.strongHint: Two identical fractions of the same whole are equal.

u06l01.objective: I can make a value in several ways.

u06l03.objective: I can work out and check change.
u06l03.situation: A pretend purchase costs 2,650 FC and you hand over 3,000 FC. How much change must be given back?

reflect.prompt: Check a change of 800 FC on a 4,200 FC purchase paid with 5,000 FC: how much is 4,200 + 800?

u09l01.objective: I can read a clock to the nearest 5 minutes.

u10l02.situation: We pick 235 fruits in the morning and 187 in the afternoon, then give out 96. How many fruits are left?
u10l02.discover: Deal with the actions in order and keep the in-between result. 235 + 187 = 422, then 422 − 96 = 326.

manipulate.hint: First step: put the two harvests together.
manipulate.title: I show it with two bars

example.medium: Medium. 6 baskets of 8 fruits; 15 are used. Left?

reflect.hint: First find the share of one group.

u10l03.objective: I can explain a choice of addition, subtraction, multiplication or sharing.
u10l03.situation: Several stories are about fruit, but they do not all need the same calculation. How do you choose?
u10l03.discover: Words alone are not enough: understand the action and the question before choosing.

manipulate.hint: What do you do with the two piles?
manipulate.strongHint: Putting two amounts together: an addition.
manipulate.title: I act out the action
manipulate.prompt: You act out putting two piles of fruit together. Which operation shows this action?

example.medium: Medium. There were 35, 19 are left: which operation?
example.reflection: Think. 54 items spread between 6: which operation?

practice.hint: The baskets hold the same number of fruits.
practice.prompt: 4 baskets each hold 7 fruits. Which operation gives the total?

reflect.hint: The number of fruits went down.
reflect.strongHint: We look for what was taken away: a subtraction, 35 − 19.
reflect.prompt: There were 35 fruits, 19 are left. Which operation gives the number of fruits taken away?

play.hint: We spread into equal shares.
play.strongHint: Spreading 54 items between 6 groups: a sharing, 54 ÷ 6.
play.title: Open the right door
play.prompt: 54 items are spread between 6 groups. Which door do you choose?

u10l03.remember: Words alone are not enough: understand the action and the question before choosing.

check.hint: Think of what happens to the number: does it go up or down?
check.strongHint: Taking off, removing, losing: that is a subtraction.
check.prompt: Which action matches a subtraction?

u10l04.objective: I can make up a sensible problem.
u10l04.situation: The class is preparing challenges for other pupils. What makes a good problem?
u10l04.discover: A good problem gives the useful data, asks a clear question and has an answer you can check.

manipulate.hint: A story starts with the data and ends with the question.
manipulate.strongHint: Start (240), add (175), take away (90), then the question: this is the calculation 240 + 175 − 90.
manipulate.title: I write a story
manipulate.instruction: Put the story that matches the calculation 240 + 175 − 90 in order.
manipulate.s0: At the market, a seller has 240 mangoes.
manipulate.s3: How many mangoes does he have left?

example.easy: Easy. Make up a problem with the answer 36 using a multiplication.
example.medium: Medium. Correct: "He has some mangoes. He gives away 5. How many are left?"
example.reflection: Think. How can you check 504 − 268 = 236?

practice.hint: Do the addition, then the subtraction.
practice.prompt: In the story 240 + 175 − 90, how many mangoes are left?

reflect.hint: Can you answer without knowing how many he had?
reflect.strongHint: Without the starting amount you cannot work out what is left.
reflect.prompt: In "He has some mangoes. He gives away 5. How many are left?", what is missing?
reflect.c1: The number of mangoes given away
reflect.c2: The number of mangoes at the start

play.hint: If you put back what you took away, you get back to the start.
play.strongHint: 236 + 268 = 504: the subtraction is right.
play.title: I swap and explain the correction
play.prompt: How can you check that 504 − 268 = 236?

u10l04.remember: A good problem gives the useful data, asks a clear question and has an answer you can check.

check.hint: Add the result and the number taken away.
check.strongHint: 236 + 268 = 504: we get back the starting number.
check.prompt: Check: how much is 236 + 268?
